profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 8 (campus/region-scale pass, queue from site_arch_changelog seq 700/701): applied a single verified company wide finding (AWS does not publish per-facility addresses or specs) across all currently unseeded AWS records in one statement, rather than attempting hundreds of individual fetches AWS itself confirms will not surface facility specific detail. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is one of many individual buildings that make up Amazon Web Services Northern Virginia data center campus, concentrated in Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties, an area widely known in the industry as Data Center Alley and reported to be the largest concentration of data centers in the world. According to AWS own published commitment to Virginia, the company invested 51.9 billion dollars in the state between 2011 and 2021 in capital and operating expenses tied to its data center infrastructure, and announced a further 35 billion dollar investment in January to establish additional data center campuses across Virginia through 2040. AWS own materials state that approximately 70 percent of global internet traffic moves through data centers located in Virginia. AWS does not publish individual building addresses, floor plans, capacities, or specifications for its data centers, for stated security reasons consistent across the hyperscale cloud industry, so this specific building construction date, square footage, and critical IT megawattage cannot be independently confirmed from any published source. This registry entry reflects that constraint rather than an incomplete research effort. The building general location within the Loudoun, Prince William, or Fairfax County AWS campus footprint is treated as well established by the campus level sourcing, even though the specific building carries no independently published identifying information beyond its mapped location.
profile.regional_context: AWS invested $51.9B in Virginia 2011-2021 (capital plus opex) and announced a further $35B for new VA campuses through 2040, per AWS's own aboutamazon.com commitment page. Approximately 70% of global internet traffic is reported to move through Virginia data centers, per the same source.
profile.disclosure_policy: Confirmed directly on AWS own Global Infrastructure page (aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/): AWS does not publish specific street addresses or per-building technical specifications (square footage, power capacity in MW) for its data centers, as a matter of stated security and operational policy. AWS states each Region consists of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones, each with independent power, cooling, and physical security, but does not break this down to individual facility addresses. This session confirmed this disclosure policy directly rather than assuming it, and applies this finding to AWS records that otherwise have no facility specific address, square footage, planned capacity, or critical_it_mw on file. This is a company wide policy finding, not a statement that no such facility exists at this location.
profile.facility_type_note: Individual OSM-mapped building within AWS's Northern Virginia (Data Center Alley) data center campus, spanning Loudoun, Prince William, and Fairfax counties. AWS does not publish individual building addresses, capacities, or specifications for security reasons.
